written.myAnswer: Compare the effort needed to move the same body over a surface with and without wheels. It is easier to move it on wheels, showing that rolling friction is much less than sliding friction—about one hundred times smaller.
Terminal velocity is the constant velocity an object reaches when air resistance balances its weight.
Without friction, we could not walk without slipping or grip objects securely. Writing and holding things would be difficult, and vehicles could not start, turn, or stop safely.

When a block is pulled across a table, static friction opposes the pull and keeps the block at rest until the pull exceeds the limiting static friction. As the block slides, kinetic friction opposes its motion. Static friction acts between surfaces that are not sliding relative to each other; kinetic friction acts between surfaces sliding against each other.

Friction between the tyres and road provides grip, helping a vehicle move and allowing braking force to slow or stop it. Tyre tread grooves help prevent a layer of water from forming between the tyre and road, reducing skidding on wet roads.
